paper_title: 1.4 Million Open-Source Distilled Reasoning Dataset to Empower Large   Language Model Training
caption: Difficulty distribution of the data entries. Most of the dataset entries are classified as Medium (51.8%) or Hard (25.7%). A smaller proportion falls into the Easy (11.2%), Very Hard (6.5%), and Very Easy (4.7%) categories.
model_annotation: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of difficulty levels across 1.4 million data entries in an open-source distilled reasoning dataset, with the title "Distribution of Difficulty." The chart is divided into five colored segments, each representing a difficulty category: Medium (51.8%, salmon pink), Hard (25.7%, blue), Easy (11.2%, light green), Very hard (6.5%, orange), and Very easy (4.7%, lavender). The largest segment, Medium, occupies more than half the circle, followed by Hard, which takes up a quarter. The remaining three categories are smaller, with Easy being the next largest, and Very hard and Very easy forming the smallest portions. Labels with percentages are placed directly on the chart next to each segment, and a legend in the upper left corner lists each difficulty level with its corresponding color and absolute count: Medium (725,892), Hard (360,137), Easy (157,053), Very hard (91,576), and Very easy (65,332). The segments are arranged clockwise starting from the top-right, with the largest segment (Medium) positioned on the left side of the chart.
